newsitem.title: USA: United Air pilots say cooperation at an end --NYT.
newsitem.headline: United Air pilots say cooperation at an end --NYT.

text.p: Leaders of the United Airlines pilots' union say they will no longer try to foster an atmosphere of cooperation at the company after recent contract negotiations, The New York Times reported on Monday.
The pilot's position is expressed in a recorded message for the members of the Air Line Pilots' Association, the newspaper said.
Union official Michael Glawe, who also serves on United's board, is quoted as saying he was "disappointed and angered" by the company's approach during recent contract negotiations.

Although the union's leaders have tentatively agreed to a wage increase to be voted on by members this month, Glawe is quoted as saying the United managers "can expect no cooperation regardless of the outcome".
The conflict marks the first public rift between the pilots and the management team they help pick for the employee-owned company, the story says.
